notes: The study was an attempt to verify a novel assay to phenotype DPYD enzyme activity. DPYD deficiency was based on monitoring endogenous dihydrouracil to uracil (UH2/U) ratio in plasma after standard liquid-liquid extraction using  HPLC-UV. notes: Patients were analyzed by HCV genotype (1,2,3,4). Patients with HCV genotype 1 were divided into groups receiving dual therapy (GT1 (d); peg-intron alpha 2a/b, ribavirn) or triple therapy (GT1 (t); peg-intron alpha 2a/b, ribavirn, telaprevir). Sustained virological response (SVR) is a measure of therapeutic efficacy. Variables that were significant in univariate analysis were included in the multivariate analysis. The authors designated three "beneficial" genotypes that were found at higher frequencies in patients who achieved SVR: rs12979860 CC, rs8099917 TT, rs368234815 TT/TT. These genotypes were often found together. 98% of patients with GT1 (d), 100% of patients with GT1(t), 96% of patients with HCV genotype 2, 92% of patients with HCV genotype 3 and 98% of patients with HCV genotype 4 had those genotype combinations.; rs12979860 CC was the only single SNP associated with SVR across all groups.  rs12979860 CC was significantly associated with SVR in GT1(d) (p<0.01). 71% of GT1(d) patients had rs12979860 CC and s368234815 TT/TT achieved SVR. In univariate analysis, the CC genotype was a significant predictor of SVR in GT1(d) as well as in patients infected with HCV genotype 2/3 (p=0.03).  The CC genotype was found to be significant in a multivariate analysis of predictive factors of SVR within all HCV genotype 1 infected patients. The CC genotype was also associated with higher HCV RNA concentration at baseline in patients with HCV genotype 3 (p<0.001), 2/3 (p<0.001) and GT1(d) (p<0.001) as well as increased ALT levels in HCV genotype 2 (p=0.026) and 2/3 patients (p=0.011).

On the branch of the pedigree that included the proband, the T allele segregated with the MHS phenotype but as a part of two distinct haplotypes. The sister of the proband inherited a TT genotype for each haplotype associated with the T allele. The mother, sister, and two sons of the proband had the T allele and the MHS phenotype. One daughter of the proband that carried the haplotype carrying the causative mutation, tested as MH negative (MHN) demonstrating possible discordance between phenotype and genotype. On the other branch of the pedigree, a father and his two sons did not carry either haplotype associated with the T allele and all three were diagnosed as MHS via IVCT. notes: A 43-yr-old woman experienced a clinically confirmed episode of malignant hyperthermia (MH) during general anaesthesia for an appendectomy. Anaesthesia was induced with thiopental and alfentanil and succinylcholine was given to facilitate orotracheal intubation. Anaesthesia was maintained with 0.6–1.0% halothane and 60% nitrous oxide in oxygen. Five minutes afterwards, she developed a tachycardia (160 bp),end-tidal [CO2] rose rapidly to 9.33 kPa temperature rose to 39.6°C. Dantrolene, was administered; post-operative serum [CK] reached 22 000 IU litre. In vitro contracture test (IVCT) confirmed the diagnosis of MH susceptibility. Genetic screening revealed that the index patient, and her sister, were homozygous (genotype TT), which is unusual since in most cases individuals are heterozygous for MHS causative mutations. The mutation was found in an additional 10 relatives in the heterozygous state. The T allele is designated as MHS causative by the European Malignant Hyperthermia Group.

In family 146 the index case was a 44 year old woman who experienced an MH episode after being administered halothane. In family 213 the index case was a 5 year old girl who experienced an MH episode after being administered halothane and succinylcholine. The rs118192172 C>T variant segregated with the MHS phenotype (as diagnosed by in vitro contracture test) in relatives of the index case in family 134. In family 146, the daughter of the index case was MHS, but did not carry the same mutation as her mother (rs118192172 C>T). notes: A 73 year old man underwent laparoscopic resection of a rectal tumor and colostomy. No serious complications arose after 4 intravenous general and three spinal anesthetics and had no experience with volatile inhalational anesthetics. At the time of surgery medication included diltiazem, lisinopril, metoprolol, famotidine, neomycin, erythromycin, and warfarin all stopped 8 days before surgery and heparin was stopped the night before surgery. The patient reported no heat sensitivity, chronic muscle aches, pain, or weakness and no family history of adverse events after anesthesia. Anesthesia was induced with 1 mg midazolam (0.014 mg/kg) and 100 mg propofol (1.4 mg/kg). Rocuronium, 50 mg (0.71 mg/kg), was used to facilitate tracheal intubation (without complication). Anesthesia continued with isoflurane (end-tidal 0.43–1.0 vol%) and intermittent doses of fentanyl, rocuronium, and hydromorphone. Heart rate was controlled with metoprolol. Ciprofloxacin and metronidazole were given before incision. Approximately 5 hours after surgery the patient began to develop symptoms of malignant hyperthermia (MH). Dantrolene was administered and the patient had to go to the ICU for several days, then back to the hospital. The patient recovered and one daughter explained that she had experienced muscle stiffness after succinylcholine and was told that she had an MH episode but never underwent contracture testing. Her father (the proband), her mother, and herself were tested for 17 known RYR1 mutations. The daughter had the CT genotype at rs118192172, while the father was compound heterozygous at rs118192172  (CT) and rs121918593 (AG). The mother did not carry any of the tested RYR1 mutations.
sentence: Genotype CT is associated with increased risk of Malignant Hyperthermia when exposed to isoflurane as compared to genotype CC.

The mutation was found in 1 index patient who experienced a clinical episode of MH under anesthesia with isoflurane- however the patient was diagnosed as MH negative (MHN) when tested with IVCT. The A allele is designated as MHS causative by the European Malignant Hyperthermia Group.
